messages.author: a5ca085497920157
messages.subject: rhgetkey
parts:
Anything happen to rhgetkey?

It is in an ambiguous state in my install.  Documentation but no function.

> ?rhgetkey
rhgetkey                 package:Rhipe                 R Documentation

Get Value Associated With a Key In A Map File

Description:

     Returns the values associated with a key in a map file on the
     HDFS.

Usage:

       rhgetkey(keys, paths, mc = lapply, size = 3000)
     
Arguments:

    keys: Keys to return values for.

   paths: Absolute path to map file on HDFS or the output from
          ârhwatchâ.

      mc: This is set to âlapplyâ, the user can set this to âmclapplyâ
          for parallel âlapplyâ

    size: Number of Key,Value pairs to increase the buffer size by at a
          time.

Value:

     Returns the values from the map files contained in âpathâ
     corresponding to the keys in âkeysâ.  âpathâ will contain folders
     which is MapFiles are stored. Thus the âpathâ must have been
     created as the output of a RHIPE job with âinout[2]â (the output
     format) set to _map_. Also, the saved keys must be in sorted
     order. This is always the case if _mapred.reduce.tasks_ is not
     zero. The variable _reduce.key_ is not modified.

Note:

     A simple way to convert any RHIPE SequenceFile data set to MapFile
     is to run an identity MapReduce.

Author(s):

     Saptarshi Guha

See Also:

     ârhgetâ, ârhputâ, ârhdelâ, ârhwriteâ, ârhsaveâ


> rhgetkey
Error: object 'rhgetkey' not found
>

messages.author: a5ca085497920157
messages.subject: Re: rhgetkey
parts: I noticed the contents of https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/blob/master/code/R/R/mapfile.functions.R,  but I couldn't get a use case to work with a single row data.frame as a key which was the form of the data I was working with.  It could have been operator error though.  I didn't give myself much time before I worked around not having rhgetkey, and I didn't cook up a test case.
